task_prompt: Analyze GitHub issue #4353 using only the fixture below (no live GitHub access). Classify the item, decide whether it duplicates one of the candidate items, and give an actionable triage summary.
input:
Repository: huggingface/accelerate ITEM #4353 Type: issue State: open Title: wait_for_everyone() raises NotImplementedError on MULTI_CPU when the machine has an MPS accelerator (barrier gets device_ids) Author: user-1 Created: 2026-09-28 Labels: (none) Body: ### System Info - accelerate: main (421af8b) — same code on v1.11.0 … v1.15.0 - torch: 2.14.0 (also reproduced with 2.8.0) - Python 3.12, macOS 24.3 (Apple Silicon, `torch.backends.mps.is_available() == True`) - No accelerate config file; `PartialState(cpu=True)` / `ACCELERATE_USE_CPU=1`, `DistributedType.MULTI_CPU` with the gloo backend ### Information - [ ] The official example scripts - [x] My own modified scripts ### Tasks - [ ] One of the scripts in the examples/ folder of Accelerate or an officially supported `no_trainer` script - [x] My own task or dataset (give details below) ### Reproduction Any multi-process CPU run on a machine that has a non-CUDA accelerator (MPS here) crashes as soon as `wait_for_everyone()` (or anything built on it, e.g. `main_process_first()`) is called: ```python # repro.py — run with: ACCELERATE_USE_CPU=1 torchrun --nproc_per_node 2 repro.py from accelerate import PartialState state = PartialState(cpu=True) print(state.distributed_type, state.device) # DistributedType.MULTI_CPU cpu:0 state.wait_for_everyone() ``` ``` NotImplementedError: The distributed operator 'c10d::barrier' is not currently implemented for the MPS device. File ".../accelerate/state.py", line 412, in wait_for_everyone torch.distributed.barrier(device_ids=[self.local_process_index]) ```
Self-contained version (spawns the two workers itself with torch.multiprocessing.spawn, no torchrun needed) ```python """ Minimal reproduction: `PartialState.wait_for_everyone()` crashes under `DistributedType.MULTI_CPU` on a machine that has a non-CUDA accelerator (e.g. Apple Silicon / MPS). Root cause: `wait_for_everyone` calls `torch.distributed.barrier(device_ids=[local_process_index])` for MULTI_CPU too. When `device_ids` is given, torch runs the barrier on `torch._C._get_accelerator()` (MPS here) instead of on the gloo/CPU device, and the MPS backend has no `c10d::barrier` -> NotImplementedError. Plain `torch.distributed.barrier()` works. Run: python repro.py """ import os import sys import traceback import torch import torch.multiprocessing as mp def worker(rank, world_size, port): os.environ.update( { "MASTER_ADDR": "127.0.0.1", "MASTER_PORT": str(port), "RANK": str(rank), "LOCAL_RANK": str(rank), "WORLD_SIZE": str(world_size), } ) from accelerate import PartialState state = PartialState(cpu=True) assert state.num_processes == world_size, state.num_processes print(f"[rank {rank}] distributed_type={state.distributed_type} device={state.device}", flush=True) try: state.wait_for_everyone() print(f"[rank {rank}] wait_for_everyone() OK", flush=True) ok = True except Exception as e: # noqa: BLE001 print(f"[rank {rank}] wait_for_everyone() FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:120]}", flush=True) traceback.print_exc(limit=1) ok = False torch.distributed.destroy_process_group() sys.exit(0 if ok else 1) if __name__ == "__main__": print(f"torch {torch.__version__}, accelerator: {torch._C._get_accelerator()}") world_size = 2 try: mp.spawn(worker, args=(world_size, 29677), nprocs=world_size, join=True) print("RESULT: PASS") except Exception as e: # noqa: BLE001 print(f"RESULT: FAIL ({type(e).__name__})") sys.exit(1) ```
What happens: since #3744, `wait_for_everyone()` passes `device_ids=[local_process_index]` to `torch.distributed.barrier()` for every distributed type, including `MULTI_CPU`. In torch's `barrier`, when `device_ids` is given the barrier device becomes `torch.device(torch._C._get_accelerator().type, device_ids[0])` — i.e. `mps:0` on a Mac — and the `_get_object_coll_device(group) == "cpu"` branch that would have picked CPU for a gloo group is skipped. MPS has no `c10d::barrier`, hence the error. Calling `torch.distributed.barrier()` without `device_ids` in the same process group works fine: ```python # gloo, 2 processes, same machine dist.barrier(device_ids=[rank]) # NotImplementedError: ... 'c10d::barrier' ... MPS dist.barrier() # OK ``` The repo's own multi-CPU test (`tests/test_cpu.py`) does not catch this because `require_cpu` skips it whenever `torch_device != "cpu"`, which is the case on any Mac with MPS. On a CUDA box the same code path would run the CPU barrier on `cuda:` (I could not verify this, no CUDA machine at hand), which at minimum initialises a CUDA context in every process of a `--cpu` run. ### Expected behavior `wait_for_everyone()` on `MULTI_CPU` should synchronise on the CPU/gloo process group regardless of which accelerator the machine happens to have, as it did before #3744. Only passing `device_ids` for the non-CPU distributed types fixes it; happy to open a PR with that one-line change plus a regression test. Disclosure: found, reproduced and the draft fix tested locally with the help of an AI coding agent (Claude Code); reviewed before filing.
